title: An expert-informed framework for participatory soundscape design: From Interviews to co-design application
why: A worked co-design experiment in participatory soundscape design, with the framework taken from expert interviews into application. A usable method template for participatory work in public space.
caveat: The framework is expert-informed and applied once. Participant outcomes are underreported.
source: Crossref topic: Participatory action research, Journal watch: Environmental Science & Policy
abstract: Participatory approaches are widely recognised in soundscape standards and policy, yet their application remains fragmented and underreported. This study developed an expert-informed conceptual framework for participatory soundscape design, with a co-design experiment demonstrating its application. Semi-structured interviews were analysed using a Straussian grounded theory analytical procedure, identifying six categories: Stakeholder roles, Soundscape design elements, Assessment and design brief, Design and demonstration, Discussion and optimisation, Documentation and validation. Stakeholder roles describe participatory soundscape design as a dynamic multi-actor process involving soundscape specialists, local experts, clients, and planning authorities. Soundscape design elements are described as multimodal, linking sound with visual-spatial context and supported by interactive audio-visual tools. The four process phases are Assessment and design brief, where stakeholders assess the soundscape and develop the design brief; Design and demonstration, where proposals are developed and compared; Discussion and optimisation, where stakeholders discuss and refine proposals; and Documentation and validation, where design process and outcomes are documented and evaluated. Overall, the framework provides insights for organising participatory soundscape design, and its applicability should be evaluated across project contexts in future studies.
